title: What Does Oud Smell Like? A Plain-English Guide to Fall's Most Divisive Note
summary: Oud is the smoky, resinous wood that forms inside some Aquilaria trees after a mold infection, and it smells warm, dark and sometimes animal. This guide explains why people love or hate it, what real and synthetic oud mean, and gives a four-step ladder from simplest to boldest.
author: Jeff Theefs
image_alt: Dark resin-streaked agarwood pieces beside three generic unbranded clear-glass 5 ml atomizers on a cream travertine ledge with folded linen and a small brass dish in warm low autumn light
seo_title: What Does Oud Smell Like? A Plain-English Guide | Base Note
seo_description: Oud smells smoky, woody, resinous and sometimes leathery. Where it comes from, real versus synthetic, and four oud fragrances from simplest to boldest.

fig-01.alt: Simple illustration showing an Aquilaria tree getting wounded, a mold getting into the wood, the tree making dark resin, and the resin-soaked wood becoming fragrant oud
fig-01.caption: A hurt tree, a mold, a protective resin: wood soaked in that resin is oud.

fig-02.alt: Four-rung ladder of oud fragrances from simplest to boldest: Tom Ford Oud Wood, Xerjoff Alexandria II, Bond No. 9 Nomad and Parfums de Marly Haltane, each with a few of its official notes
fig-02.caption: Rungs rise from the simplest blend to the two whose makers call them strong or powerful; the ladder does not rank projection.

fig-03.alt: Close-up of dark agarwood with deep brown resin streaks running through pale wood grain and a thin wisp of smoke in warm autumn light
